gloss: all beasts; all animals; every kind of beast

definitions.gloss: all beasts; all animals; every kind of beast

examples.japanese: ライオンは{百獣|ひゃくじゅう}の{王|おう}だ。
examples.english: The lion is the king of beasts.

examples.japanese: {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}の{王|おう}と{呼|よ}ばれるライオンにも{天敵|てんてき}はいる。
examples.english: Even the lion, called the king of beasts, has natural enemies.

examples.japanese: {古代|こだい}の{神話|しんわ}では、{百獣|ひゃくじゅう}を{従|したが}える{神|かみ}の{物語|ものがたり}が{数多|かずおお}く{語|かた}られている。
examples.english: In ancient mythology, there are many stories told of gods who commanded all the beasts.

notes:
A literary term where {百|ひゃく} means "all" or "many" (not literally one hundred) and {獣|じゅう} means "beast." Most commonly encountered in the set phrase {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}の{王|おう} (king of beasts).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}の{王|おう}: king of beasts (referring to the lion)
- {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}を{従|したが}える: to command all beasts

CULTURAL NOTE:
The phrase {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}の{王|おう} appears in anime, manga, and television. The professional wrestler and mixed martial artist Akira Maeda was famously nicknamed {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}の{王|おう}. The concept also features in various Japanese card games and fantasy media.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {野獣|やじゅう}: wild beast — refers to specific savage animals
- {猛獣|もうじゅう}: fierce beast, dangerous animal — emphasizes danger
- {動物|どうぶつ}: animal — the general, everyday word
